```plato

    //==
    // # Rewriting the vertex array — the seam purity is paid at
    //
    // Constraint projection is naturally in-place: a solver writes two vertices
    // and moves on. Plato has no in-place write to an `Array`, so each
    // projection below returns a NEW vertex array with the touched entries
    // replaced, built by a single `MapRange` over the old one.
    //
    // That is the whole cost of doing this purely, and it is worth stating
    // plainly: one projection is O(vertex count) rather than O(1), so one
    // Gauss-Seidel sweep is O(vertices * constraints) where the in-place
    // version is O(constraints). Nothing else about the algorithm changes —
    // the arithmetic, the convergence and the results are identical.
    //
    // The affine builder `Buffer<ClothVertex>` (`primitives.plato`) would give
    // the in-place cost back and stay pure by uniqueness, but it cannot drive
    // this loop: a builder may not be captured in a lambda or used as a generic
    // argument (LINT006 / LINT007), and Plato has no loop form, so there is no
    // way to sweep a constraint array over one. See the sweep section below for
    // the alternative that IS available.

    // The vertex array with one vertex replaced.
    WithVertex(self: Array<ClothVertex>, index: VertexIndex, vertex: ClothVertex): Array<ClothVertex>
        => self.Count.MapRange(i => i == index.Value ? vertex : self[i]);
```
